edits.why: version statement: the tutorial now targets SQLAlchemy 2.1

edits.old: The metadata is bound with `MetaData(bind=engine)`, so `create_all` needs no argument.
edits.new: The metadata is created with `MetaData()`, so `create_all` takes the engine.
edits.why: MetaData(bind=...) was removed; the engine is passed to create_all

edits.old: Check the table with `engine.table_names()` at the end.
edits.new: Check the table with `inspect(engine).get_table_names()` at the end.
edits.why: Engine.table_names was removed in favour of the inspector

edits.old: In SQLAlchemy 1.4, `engine.execute` runs a statement directly.
edits.new: In SQLAlchemy 2.1, `conn.execute` runs a statement on a connection.
edits.why: Engine.execute was removed; statements run on a connection

edits.old: by calling `select` on a list of columns.
edits.why: select([...]) with a list was removed; columns are positional

edits.old: then read the low items by name with `row['name']`.
edits.new: then read the low items by name with `row._mapping['name']`.
edits.why: Row no longer supports string indexing; use the mapping
